authors: Samuelson, P.A.
title: Lifetime Portfolio Selection by Dynamic Stochastic Programming
key_finding: Solves the many-period investment problem step by step. If returns are unpredictable and risk attitude does not depend on wealth, a longer horizon by itself is no reason to hold more risky assets.
why_it_matters_for_daa: It is the benchmark case in which a fixed mix is optimal, so any dynamic strategy must explain which of its assumptions fails.

authors: Merton, R.C.
title: Lifetime Portfolio Selection under Uncertainty: The Continuous-Time Case
key_finding: In continuous time with constant investment opportunities, the best share in risky assets is constant and does not depend on the horizon.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Defines the 'constant-mix' baseline that tactical and dynamic tilts are measured against.

authors: Merton, R.C.
title: An Intertemporal Capital Asset Pricing Model
key_finding: When investment opportunities change over time, investors also hold 'hedging' positions against bad shifts in future returns, and expected returns reflect exposure to those state variables.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Gives the theoretical reason why the optimal mix should move when expected returns or risk change.

authors: Brinson, G.P.; Hood, L.R.; Beebower, G.L.
title: Determinants of Portfolio Performance
key_finding: For 91 US pension funds in 1974-83, the policy mix explained about 94% of the variation in quarterly returns over time; market timing and security selection added little and on average cost money.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Sets the bar: tactical decisions have historically been a small and often negative contributor, so a DAA programme must prove it adds value.

authors: Perold, A.F.; Sharpe, W.F.
title: Dynamic Strategies for Asset Allocation
key_finding: Compares buy-and-hold, constant-mix rebalancing and portfolio-insurance rules. Rebalancing wins in choppy, trendless markets; insurance-style rules that buy winners win in trending markets.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Shows every dynamic rule is an implicit bet on the type of market ahead (mean-reverting versus trending).

authors: Ibbotson, R.G.; Kaplan, P.D.
title: Does Asset Allocation Policy Explain 40, 90, or 100 Percent of Performance?
key_finding: Policy mix explains about 90% of a fund's return swings over time, about 40% of the differences between funds, and about 100% of the average return level.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Clarifies how much room active allocation decisions really have to change outcomes.

authors: Barberis, N.
title: Investing for the Long Run when Returns Are Predictable
key_finding: Return predictability pushes long-horizon investors toward more equity, but uncertainty about the model's parameters cuts that effect substantially; ignoring it leads to over-investment.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A key argument for keeping timing bets modest when the evidence for predictability is uncertain.

authors: Campbell, J.Y.; Viceira, L.M.
title: Strategic Asset Allocation: Portfolio Choice for Long-Term Investors
key_finding: Long-term investors should hedge changes in investment opportunities; inflation-indexed bonds are the long-run safe asset, and mean reversion can make stocks less risky over long horizons.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The standard bridge between intertemporal theory and practical, time-varying allocation for long-horizon funds.

authors: Fama, E.F.; French, K.R.
title: Dividend Yields and Expected Stock Returns
key_finding: Dividend yields forecast stock returns; the forecasting power is small at monthly horizons but grows a lot at multi-year horizons.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Founding evidence that valuation tells you more about long-run than short-run returns.

authors: Campbell, J.Y.; Shiller, R.J.
title: Valuation Ratios and the Long-Run Stock Market Outlook
key_finding: Smoothed price-earnings (CAPE-style) and dividend-price ratios forecast future price changes rather than earnings or dividend growth; high valuations pointed to weak ten-year returns.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Basis of CAPE-style valuation signals used for long-horizon tilts and capital-market assumptions.

authors: Cochrane, J.H.
title: The Dog That Did Not Bark: A Defense of Return Predictability
key_finding: If returns were unpredictable, dividend growth would have to be predictable from prices, and it is not; that gives strong joint evidence that expected returns vary over time.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The main theoretical defence of time-varying expected returns, the premise behind tactical allocation.

authors: Welch, I.; Goyal, A.
title: A Comprehensive Look at the Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
key_finding: Popular equity-premium predictors were unstable and mostly failed to beat the simple historical average when used in real time (out of sample).
why_it_matters_for_daa: The classic warning that in-sample predictability rarely survives real-time use.

authors: Goyal, A.; Welch, I.; Zafirov, A.
title: A Comprehensive 2022 Look at the Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
key_finding: Re-tests the original predictors plus 29 newer ones with data through 2021: over a third lose in-sample significance, about half of the rest fail out of sample, and only a few hold up.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Up-to-date evidence that single-variable market timing remains fragile, so signals must be combined and sized cautiously.

authors: Campbell, J.Y.; Thompson, S.B.
title: Predicting Excess Stock Returns Out of Sample: Can Anything Beat the Historical Average?
key_finding: Simple common-sense restrictions, such as ruling out a negative expected equity premium, let many predictors beat the historical mean; the gain in forecast accuracy is small but economically meaningful.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Shows that small, well-constrained forecasts can still be worth acting on through modest tilts.

authors: Asness, C.S.
title: Fight the Fed Model
key_finding: The popular 'Fed model' compares a real earnings yield with a nominal bond yield, which is conceptually flawed, and it does not forecast long-term stock returns; traditional valuation measures do better.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A caution against intuitive but mis-specified valuation signals when comparing stocks and bonds.

authors: Asness, C.; Ilmanen, A.; Maloney, T.
title: Market Timing: Sin a Little - Resolving the Valuation Timing Puzzle
key_finding: Contrarian valuation timing of equities disappointed in practice; combining value with momentum supported only modest tilts around the normal equity weight.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Practical guidance on sizing: valuation views justify small, disciplined deviations, not big bets.

authors: Ilmanen, A.
title: Expected Returns: An Investor's Guide to Harvesting Market Rewards
key_finding: A broad survey of the evidence on expected returns across asset-class premia, style factors and strategies, using history, theory and forward-looking indicators.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A practitioner reference for building the expected-return inputs that drive allocation decisions.

authors: Koijen, R.S.J.; Moskowitz, T.J.; Pedersen, L.H.; Vrugt, E.B.
title: Carry
key_finding: An asset's 'carry' (what it earns if prices do not change) predicts returns across equities, bonds, currencies, commodities, credit and options, both across assets and over time.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Carry is a model-free, observable signal that complements value and trend in a cross-asset tactical toolkit.

authors: Faber, M.T.
title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
key_finding: Holding each of five asset classes only when its price is above its 10-month moving average (otherwise cash) delivered equity-like returns with bond-like volatility and much smaller drawdowns.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The simplest widely cited trend overlay, and a natural baseline for any tactical rule.

authors: Blitz, D.; van Vliet, P.
title: Global Tactical Cross-Asset Allocation: Applying Value and Momentum Across Asset Classes
key_finding: Combining value and momentum signals across 12 asset classes earned about 9% a year long-short in 1986-2007, not explained by standard risk factors.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Early academic evidence that cross-asset tactical signals can add value, especially when combined.

authors: Moskowitz, T.J.; Ooi, Y.H.; Pedersen, L.H.
title: Time Series Momentum
key_finding: In 58 futures markets, an asset's own past 12-month return predicts its next returns; a diversified trend portfolio earned large alpha and did best in extreme up and down markets.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The core academic evidence for trend-following as a cross-asset tactical signal.

authors: Asness, C.S.; Moskowitz, T.J.; Pedersen, L.H.
title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
key_finding: Value and momentum premia appear in eight markets and asset classes; the two are negatively correlated, so combining them is much smoother than either alone.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Supports running value and momentum together across asset classes rather than choosing one.

authors: Hurst, B.; Ooi, Y.H.; Pedersen, L.H.
title: A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing
key_finding: Trend following across 67 markets was profitable for more than a century, with low correlation to stocks and bonds and good results in equity bear markets.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Long-history evidence that trend is a durable diversifier rather than a recent backtest artefact.

authors: Antonacci, G.
title: Dual Momentum Investing: An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk
key_finding: Combines relative momentum (pick the stronger asset) with absolute momentum (exit to bonds or bills when excess return is negative) to switch between equities and safer assets.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A transparent, rules-based template (Global Equities Momentum) for combining selection and trend filters.

authors: Keller, W.J.; van Putten, H.
title: Generalized Momentum and Flexible Asset Allocation (FAA): An Heuristic Approach
key_finding: Ranks assets on a blend of relative return, absolute momentum, volatility and correlation, and holds the top-ranked ones; tested on seven assets from 1998 to 2012.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Shows how risk and correlation can be folded into a momentum ranking in a simple heuristic.

authors: Keller, W.J.; Butler, A.; Kipnis, I.
title: Momentum and Markowitz: A Golden Combination
key_finding: Feeds short-lookback (momentum-style) estimates of returns, volatilities and correlations into mean-variance optimisation, producing a correlation-aware tactical allocation (Classical Asset Allocation).
why_it_matters_for_daa: Bridges trend signals and portfolio optimisation, the same idea behind adaptive asset allocation.

authors: Keller, W.J.; Keuning, J.W.
title: Protective Asset Allocation (PAA): A Simple Momentum-Based Alternative for Term Deposits
key_finding: Dual momentum with 'breadth' crash protection: the share in bonds or cash rises as fewer risky assets show positive momentum.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Introduces market breadth as a defensive signal for scaling total risk.

authors: Keller, W.J.; Keuning, J.W.
title: Breadth Momentum and Vigilant Asset Allocation (VAA): Winning More by Losing Less
key_finding: Uses a fast momentum score (weighted 1/3/6/12-month returns) and a strict breadth rule that moves to cash when any risky asset turns negative, aiming for high returns with shallow drawdowns.
why_it_matters_for_daa: An aggressive defensive rule that shows the trade-off between crash protection and time spent in cash.

authors: Keller, W.J.; Keuning, J.W.
title: Breadth Momentum and the Canary Universe: Defensive Asset Allocation (DAA)
key_finding: Uses a separate 'canary' set of assets (e.g., emerging-market equities and aggregate bonds) to trigger crash protection, holding far less cash than VAA with similar return and risk.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Separating the risk-off signal from the investment universe is a useful design pattern for overlays.

authors: Baltas, N.; Kosowski, R.
title: Demystifying Time-Series Momentum Strategies: Volatility Estimators, Trading Rules and Pairwise Correlations
venue: Chapter 3 in Market Momentum: Theory and Practice, Wiley (book chapter)
key_finding: Better volatility estimators and trend signals cut turnover; weaker trend results after 2008 are linked to rising correlations between assets, and a correlation-based leverage adjustment helps.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Implementation details (volatility estimation, correlation) matter as much as the trend signal itself.

authors: Levine, A.; Pedersen, L.H.
title: Which Trend Is Your Friend?
key_finding: Time-series momentum and moving-average crossover rules are closely related in theory and data; the authors introduce 'trend signature plots' to compare them.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Tells a DAA team that the choice of exact trend rule matters less than diversification across speeds and markets.

authors: Huang, D.; Li, J.; Wang, L.; Zhou, G.
title: Time Series Momentum: Is It There?
key_finding: Asset by asset, there is little evidence that past 12-month returns predict future returns; trend-strategy profits are roughly matched by a rule based on each asset's historical average return.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The main academic critique of trend following, a reminder to test whether a signal adds value beyond simple averages.

authors: Clare, A.; Seaton, J.; Smith, P.N.; Thomas, S.
title: The Trend Is Our Friend: Risk Parity, Momentum and Trend Following in Global Asset Allocation
venue: Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance 9
key_finding: Compares and combines risk parity, cross-asset momentum and trend following in global allocation; trend following is the key ingredient for better risk-adjusted returns and smaller drawdowns.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Direct evidence for blending risk-based weighting with a trend filter.

authors: Hamilton, J.D.
title: A New Approach to the Economic Analysis of Nonstationary Time Series and the Business Cycle
key_finding: Introduces the Markov regime-switching model, in which the economy moves between hidden states such as expansion and recession with different behaviour.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The workhorse statistical tool behind most regime-based allocation models.

authors: Ang, A.; Bekaert, G.
title: International Asset Allocation with Regime Shifts
key_finding: In bear regimes volatility and correlations rise; even so, international diversification still pays under regime shifts, and currency hedging adds value.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Shows that correlations are regime-dependent, which matters for sizing and hedging in stress periods.

authors: Kritzman, M.; Page, S.; Turkington, D.
title: Regime Shifts: Implications for Dynamic Strategies
key_finding: Regime models of market turbulence, inflation and growth guided dynamic risk-premia and stock-bond-cash allocations that beat static ones out of sample, mainly by limiting large losses.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A practitioner-ready template for regime-aware tilts focused on downside protection.

authors: Ilmanen, A.; Maloney, T.; Ross, A.
title: Exploring Macroeconomic Sensitivities: How Investments Respond to Different Economic Environments
key_finding: Asset-class returns depend heavily on growth and inflation environments, while style premia (value, momentum, carry, defensive) are far less sensitive to the macro backdrop.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Supports mapping the fund to growth and inflation exposures and using style premia to diversify macro risk.

authors: Harvey, C.R.; Hoyle, E.; Rattray, S.; Sargaison, M.; Taylor, D.; Van Hemert, O.
title: The Best of Strategies for the Worst of Times: Can Portfolios Be Crisis Proofed?
key_finding: Over 1985-2018, buying put options protected reliably but was very costly, Treasuries were an unreliable hedge, and trend following and quality long-short strategies gave the best crisis protection.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Guides which defensive overlays a fund should hold for equity sell-offs.

authors: Neville, H.; Draaisma, T.; Funnell, B.; Harvey, C.R.; Van Hemert, O.
title: The Best Strategies for Inflationary Times
key_finding: Across about a century of US, UK and Japanese data, unexpected inflation hurt both equities and nominal bonds, while commodities and trend-following strategies protected best.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Evidence base for an inflation overlay, which proved directly relevant in 2021-2022.

authors: Campbell, J.Y.; Pflueger, C.; Viceira, L.M.
title: Macroeconomic Drivers of Bond and Equity Risks
key_finding: Around 2001 the link between inflation and output shifted, which turned the stock-bond correlation negative; time-varying risk premia amplify this effect.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Explains why the bond hedge for equities depends on the macro regime and can switch off.

authors: Brooks, J.
title: A Half Century of Macro Momentum
key_finding: A systematic strategy that goes long assets whose fundamental macro trends are improving and short those deteriorating; a backtest since 1970 suggested diversification benefits in equity drawdowns and rising-yield periods.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Shows how macro data (not just prices) can drive cross-asset tactical positions.

authors: Mulliner, A.; Harvey, C.R.; Xia, C.; Fang, E.; Van Hemert, O.
title: Regimes
key_finding: Identifies past dates whose economic conditions (seven state variables) most resemble today and positions on what happened next; reports strong factor-timing results and finds the least similar periods informative too.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A transparent, similarity-based alternative to hidden-state regime models.

authors: Costa, M.; Sueppel, R.
title: A macro-quantamental scorecard for global equity allocation
key_finding: Builds a scorecard from point-in-time macro indicators to tilt country equity weights; across 19 markets the scores showed significant predictive power and positive returns from cross-country allocation.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Example of practitioner 'macro-quantamental' signals that use only data available at each date.

authors: Qian, E.
title: Risk Parity Portfolios: Efficient Portfolios Through True Diversification
key_finding: A 60/40 portfolio gets roughly 90% of its risk from stocks; balancing risk across asset classes gives truer diversification and better risk-adjusted returns.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Origin of 'risk parity', a common baseline for risk-based allocation.

authors: Maillard, S.; Roncalli, T.; Teiletche, J.
title: The Properties of Equally Weighted Risk Contribution Portfolios
key_finding: Formally defines the equal-risk-contribution portfolio, shows it has a unique solution, and that its volatility lies between the minimum-variance and equal-weight portfolios.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The standard technical reference for implementing risk parity.

authors: Asness, C.S.; Frazzini, A.; Pedersen, L.H.
title: Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity
key_finding: Because many investors avoid leverage, safer assets offer better risk-adjusted returns; a leveraged risk-parity portfolio beat the market at equal risk over 1926-2010.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Explains why risk-balanced, levered portfolios can work and why leverage capacity is a strategic asset for large funds.

authors: Moreira, A.; Muir, T.
title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
key_finding: Scaling exposure down when recent volatility is high (and up when it is low) produced alphas and higher Sharpe ratios for the market and many factors.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Influential evidence for volatility-scaled exposure as a dynamic rule.

authors: Harvey, C.R.; Hoyle, E.; Korgaonkar, R.; Rattray, S.; Sargaison, M.; Van Hemert, O.
title: The Impact of Volatility Targeting
key_finding: Across 60+ assets since 1926, volatility targeting reduced extreme tail events and raised Sharpe ratios for equities and credit, but not for bonds or commodities.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Shows where volatility targeting helps (risk assets) and where it does not.

authors: Cederburg, S.; O'Doherty, M.S.; Wang, F.; Yan, X.
title: On the Performance of Volatility-Managed Portfolios
key_finding: Across 103 equity strategies, volatility-managed versions did not reliably beat the originals when implemented realistically out of sample.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A key critique: volatility scaling is a risk tool, not a guaranteed return enhancer.

authors: Grossman, S.J.; Zhou, Z.
title: Optimal Investment Strategies for Controlling Drawdowns
key_finding: If wealth must never fall below a fixed fraction of its past peak, the optimal risky exposure is proportional to the cushion above that moving floor.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The theoretical basis for drawdown-control overlays and their pro-cyclical behaviour.

authors: Ang, A.
title: Asset Management: A Systematic Approach to Factor Investing
key_finding: Asset classes are bundles of factor risks; factor premia reward investors for bearing losses in bad times, so allocation should target factors rather than labels.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The intellectual foundation for factor-based, total-fund allocation at large asset owners.

authors: Idzorek, T.M.; Kowara, M.
title: Factor-Based Asset Allocation vs. Asset-Class-Based Asset Allocation
key_finding: Neither approach is inherently superior; claims that factor allocation wins usually come from unfair comparisons such as allowing shorting for factors but not for asset classes.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A healthy check: the value of a factor lens is clearer risk thinking, not automatic outperformance.

authors: Bass, R.; Gladstone, S.; Ang, A.
title: Total Portfolio Factor, Not Just Asset, Allocation
key_finding: Measure the whole portfolio's exposure to macro factors such as growth, real rates and inflation, then choose the assets that deliver the target exposures.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A practical recipe for a total-fund factor view across public and private holdings.

authors: Ang, A.; Brandt, M.W.; Denison, D.F.
title: Review of the Active Management of the Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global
venue: Report to the Norwegian Ministry of Finance
key_finding: Reviews the fund's active management and recommends systematic factor harvesting and a CPPIB-style reference-portfolio ('opportunity cost') model for setting and judging risk.
why_it_matters_for_daa: An influential public blueprint for how a very large fund can organise total-portfolio decisions.

authors: Beath, A.D.; Betermier, S.; Flynn, C.; Spehner, Q.
title: The Canadian Pension Fund Model: A Quantitative Portrait
venue: Journal of Portfolio Management (Investment Models special issue 2021)
key_finding: Over 2004-2018, large Canadian pension funds beat global peers on returns and liability hedging, helped by in-house management, internal teams and tilts toward private and strategic assets.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Documents the 'Canadian model' that a Canadian pension DAA team operates within.

authors: CPP Investments
title: Statement of Investment Objectives, Policies, Return Expectations and Risk Management for the Investment Portfolios of the Base Canada Pension Plan and the Additional Canada Pension Plan
key_finding: Each portfolio targets the risk level of a simple two-index Reference Portfolio (85% global equity and 15% Canadian government bonds for the base plan), with performance also judged against a benchmark portfolio.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A primary-source example of the reference-portfolio approach used by a large Canadian fund.

authors: Guardians of New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super Fund)
title: Reference Portfolio
key_finding: Describes a notional, low-cost listed portfolio of 80% growth and 20% fixed income assets used as the benchmark for the actual portfolio and for measuring active value-add.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Shows how a reference portfolio separates the board's risk decision from active total-fund decisions.

authors: Black, F.; Litterman, R.
title: Global Portfolio Optimization
key_finding: Starts from market-equilibrium returns as a neutral anchor and blends in investor views in proportion to confidence, avoiding the extreme portfolios of plain mean-variance optimisation.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Still the standard Bayesian way to turn tactical views into sensible, bounded tilts.

authors: Gu, S.; Kelly, B.; Xiu, D.
title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
key_finding: Tree models and neural networks forecast stock returns better than linear regressions by capturing non-linear interactions, in some cases doubling strategy performance.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The benchmark study for ML in return prediction, though it relies on large cross-sections that tactical allocation lacks.

authors: Kelly, B.; Malamud, S.; Zhou, K.
title: The Virtue of Complexity in Return Prediction
key_finding: Theory and US market-timing evidence suggest models with more parameters than observations can beat simple models in return prediction and portfolio Sharpe ratio.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Challenges the 'keep timing models simple' rule and sparked a major 2025 debate.

authors: Nagel, S.
title: Seemingly Virtuous Complexity in Return Prediction
key_finding: With short training windows, the complex random-feature forecast behaves like volatility-timed momentum, so its apparent success reflects momentum rather than genuine learning from complexity.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A caution to look inside complex models and check whether a simple known signal explains them.

authors: Jensen, T.I.; Kelly, B.; Malamud, S.; Pedersen, L.H.
title: Machine Learning and the Implementable Efficient Frontier
venue: Review of Financial Studies (in press; SSRN 2022)
key_finding: ML portfolios that ignore trading costs chase short-lived signals; learning portfolio weights directly with costs built in gives a better after-cost frontier.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Any ML-driven tilt must be judged after costs and turnover, not on gross forecasts.

authors: Bybee, L.; Kelly, B.; Manela, A.; Xiu, D.
title: Business News and Business Cycles
key_finding: A topic model of about 800,000 Wall Street Journal articles (1984-2017) shows that news attention to themes tracks and helps explain aggregate economic activity and market returns.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A rigorous step toward text-based macro signals for top-down allocation.

authors: Lopez-Lira, A.; Tang, Y.
title: Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models
key_finding: Large-language-model sentiment scores on news headlines predict subsequent stock returns, most strongly for small stocks and after negative news.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Early evidence that LLMs can extract tradable information from text, the basis for LLM-driven macro research.

authors: Sarkar, S.K.; Vafa, K.
title: Lookahead Bias in Pretrained Language Models
key_finding: Directly detects look-ahead bias in LLM forecasts (models 'know' outcomes from their training data); prompting is a weak fix, so models trained only on earlier text are needed.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Any LLM-based macro backtest must be tested on data after the model's training cut-off.

authors: Sullivan, R.; Timmermann, A.; White, H.
title: Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap
key_finding: Testing thousands of technical rules on 100 years of Dow Jones data, apparent outperformance largely disappears once the number of rules tried and out-of-sample data are taken into account.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Directly relevant to rule-based tactical strategies: the best of many rules looks good by chance.

authors: Bailey, D.H.; Lopez de Prado, M.
title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality
key_finding: Adjusts a backtest Sharpe ratio for the number of strategies tried, the spread of their results, sample length, skew and fat tails, to separate real findings from flukes.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A practical statistic for deciding whether a selected strategy variant is genuinely good.

authors: Bailey, D.H.; Borwein, J.M.; Lopez de Prado, M.; Zhu, Q.J.
title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
key_finding: Defines the probability that the best in-sample strategy underperforms out of sample and estimates it with combinatorially symmetric cross-validation.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Gives a measurable overfitting risk for any selection process among strategy variants.

authors: Harvey, C.R.; Liu, Y.; Zhu, H.
title: ...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
key_finding: After hundreds of factors have been tested, a new one should clear a t-statistic of about 3 rather than 2; many published findings are likely false positives.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Raises the evidence bar for adopting any new tactical signal.

authors: McLean, R.D.; Pontiff, J.
title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
key_finding: Across 97 predictors, returns were about 26% lower out of sample and about 58% lower after publication, consistent with both overfitting and investors trading on published ideas.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Expect live results from published signals to be well below their backtests.

authors: Arnott, R.D.; Harvey, C.R.; Markowitz, H.
title: A Backtesting Protocol in the Era of Machine Learning
key_finding: A seven-part checklist: state the hypothesis before looking at data, account for multiple tests, be careful with sample choice, and beware overfitting given finance's small data.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A ready-made research governance standard for a DAA team.

authors: Jensen, T.I.; Kelly, B.; Pedersen, L.H.
title: Is There a Replication Crisis in Finance?
key_finding: Using a Bayesian approach on 153 factors in 93 countries, most factors replicate, group into 13 themes, and work out of sample.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Balances the overfitting critiques: well-grounded factor themes do persist.

authors: Suhonen, A.; Lennkh, M.; Perez, F.
title: Quantifying Backtest Overfitting in Alternative Beta Strategies
key_finding: Across 215 bank 'alternative beta' strategies, the median Sharpe ratio fell from 1.20 in backtests to 0.31 live (about a 73% haircut), and more complex strategies decayed more.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A concrete haircut to apply when evaluating externally offered systematic strategies.

authors: Bates, J.M.; Granger, C.W.J.
title: The Combination of Forecasts
key_finding: Combining two forecasts, weighted by their past errors, can produce smaller errors than either forecast alone.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The founding idea behind blending many weak tactical signals.

authors: Timmermann, A.
title: Forecast Combinations
venue: Handbook of Economic Forecasting, Vol. 1 (Elsevier), Chapter 4
key_finding: Combinations usually beat the best single model chosen in advance, and simple equal weights often beat estimated 'optimal' weights.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Supports simple, robust weighting of signals rather than heavily optimised blends.

authors: Rapach, D.E.; Strauss, J.K.; Zhou, G.
title: Out-of-Sample Equity Premium Prediction: Combination Forecasts and Links to the Real Economy
key_finding: Averaging forecasts from many individual predictors beats the historical mean out of sample, even though single predictors fail, and the gains are linked to business-cycle conditions.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The direct answer to Welch-Goyal: combining weak predictors makes timing more reliable.

authors: DeMiguel, V.; Garlappi, L.; Uppal, R.
title: Optimal Versus Naive Diversification: How Inefficient Is the 1/N Portfolio Strategy?
key_finding: None of 14 optimised portfolio models consistently beat simple equal weighting out of sample, because estimation errors eat the theoretical gains.
why_it_matters_for_daa: A reminder to benchmark any optimised blend against simple equal weights.

authors: Tu, J.; Zhou, G.
title: Markowitz Meets Talmud: A Combination of Sophisticated and Naive Diversification Strategies
key_finding: Optimally mixing equal weights with sophisticated rules improves the sophisticated rules and usually beats equal weighting.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Supports shrinking optimised strategy weights toward equal weights.

authors: Fitzgibbons, S.; Friedman, J.; Pomorski, L.; Serban, L.
title: Long-Only Style Investing: Don't Just Mix, Integrate
key_finding: Combining style signals into one score before building the portfolio beats mixing separate single-style portfolios in long-only investing.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Informs whether to blend signals or blend sub-portfolios in a multi-signal overlay.

authors: Ghayur, K.; Heaney, R.; Platt, S.
title: Constructing Long-Only Multifactor Strategies: Portfolio Blending vs. Signal Blending
key_finding: Blending portfolios gives better information ratios at low to moderate factor exposure, while blending signals wins at high exposure.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The right combination method depends on the risk budget for active tilts.

authors: Dichtl, H.; Drobetz, W.; Lohre, H.; Rother, C.; Vosskamp, P.
title: Optimal Timing and Tilting of Equity Factors
key_finding: Factor returns are somewhat predictable, but after costs, timing adds only modest value over equal weighting and tilting adds little.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Tempers expectations for dynamically re-weighting a set of strategies.

authors: Rattray, S.; Granger, N.; Harvey, C.R.; Van Hemert, O.
title: Strategic Rebalancing
key_finding: Mechanical rebalancing hurts in trending crises because it keeps buying the falling asset; adding trend following, or delaying rebalancing when trend signals are negative, reduces 60/40 drawdowns.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Directly relevant to a total-fund team that owns rebalancing: combine it with trend to avoid its built-in weakness.

authors: Brixton, A.; Brooks, J.; Hecht, P.; Ilmanen, A.; Maloney, T.; McQuinn, N.
title: A Changing Stock-Bond Correlation: Drivers and Implications
key_finding: The stock-bond correlation depends on whether growth or inflation uncertainty dominates, not on the inflation level; moving from -0.5 to +0.5 raises 60/40 volatility by about one-fifth.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Post-2022 the bond hedge cannot be assumed; correlation must be monitored and planned for.

authors: Molenaar, R.; Senechal, E.; Swinkels, L.; Wang, Z.
title: Empirical Evidence on the Stock-Bond Correlation
key_finding: With data back to 1875, a positive stock-bond correlation has been common; inflation, real rates and sovereign credit risk drive it, and shifts between regimes can be abrupt.
why_it_matters_for_daa: The negative correlation of 2000-2021 was the exception, so diversification assumptions need regime awareness.

authors: Pinter, G.
title: An anatomy of the 2022 gilt market crisis
venue: Bank of England Staff Working Paper No. 1,019
key_finding: Forced selling by leveraged liability-driven investment funds, linked to repo and derivative positions, drained liquidity in long-dated and index-linked gilts, and the costs spread to other investors.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Shows how pension leverage can turn a rate shock into a liquidity crisis, so collateral planning is part of DAA.

authors: Plong, B.; Maru, N.
title: What has been putting upward pressure on CORRA?
venue: Bank of Canada Staff Analytical Note 2024-4
key_finding: Documents that large Canadian pension funds use leverage heavily, funding large fixed-income holdings through repo with dealers and using repo for cash needs and bridge financing.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Leverage and repo funding are integral to Canadian pension portfolios, so funding conditions matter for total-fund management.

authors: Fontaine, J.-S.; Tchamova, S.; Maru, N.
title: A buoy on funding tides: How client repo demand and dealer constraints lifted CORRA
venue: Bank of Canada Staff Analytical Paper 2026-15
key_finding: In fall 2025, pension plans led an initial drop in repo cash lending while hedge funds borrowed more, pushing up Canada's overnight repo rate (CORRA).
why_it_matters_for_daa: Recent evidence that pension liquidity and funding decisions move short-term funding markets.

authors: Stafford, E.
title: Replicating Private Equity with Value Investing, Homemade Leverage, and Hold-to-Maturity Accounting
key_finding: A portfolio of small, cheap public stocks with modest leverage and hold-to-maturity (smoothed) valuation replicates pre-fee private-equity returns.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Helps a total-fund team see through private-asset smoothing to the underlying public-market factor exposures.

authors: CAIA Association; Future Fund; CPP Investments; NZ Super Fund; GIC
title: Innovation Unleashed: The Rise of Total Portfolio Approach
key_finding: Under the Total Portfolio Approach, success is judged by total-fund return within an overall risk budget rather than by asset-class benchmarks, with diversification framed by factors rather than asset classes.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Describes the governance model in which a total-fund DAA team operates at leading asset owners.

authors: CAIA Association; WTW Thinking Ahead Institute
title: From Vision to Execution: How Investors Are Operationalizing the Total Portfolio Approach
venue: CAIA Association / Thinking Ahead Institute report
key_finding: Based on discussions with about a dozen asset owners, maps the stages of moving from strategic asset allocation to TPA and finds the main hurdles are culture and governance rather than resources.
why_it_matters_for_daa: Practical, current view of how funds actually implement total-portfolio decision-making.
